deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The page is a log of pendulum or oscillator timings. It is headed 'Versuche ♀ Mai 6 [1836]'. ♀ means Friday, and 6 May 1836 was indeed a Friday (day 127 of a year that began on a Friday; 126 ≡ 0 mod 7).

The header defines two observing set-ups and their orientation conventions.
- I: the middle of a swing from East to West. Seen with the naked eye, the 'Tüte' (a cone or marker on the oscillating body) moves right to left. In the telescope it moves left to right, because the telescope inverts the image.
- II: the middle of a swing from South to North, observed via the mirror image of a scale line ('Spiegelbild des Strichs'). To the naked eye it sinks; in the telescope it rises. 'Nord' was first written and struck out.

The lower part gives clock times (h.m.s) against swing counts.
- Counts with the same fractional part are 4 s apart per unit, i.e. one count unit ≈ 4.000 s.
- Series II counts mostly at n.5, and its elongations at n.25 and n.75. This suggests the counting unit is a full period: middle passages at the half-units, turning points at the quarter-units.
- These definitions serve to fix unambiguously which passage is being timed.

SERIES I (E→W passages). Times and counts:
- 22h8m9.2s→128, 21.2→131, 33.2→134 (12 s per 3 units);
- 22.11.45.28→182, 53.28→184, 22.12.1.32→186;
- 0.20.12.60→2109 (written over; machine-read '2009'), 20.56→2111, 28.60→2113;
- 0.48.12.40→2529, 28.40→2533 (machine-read '2537'), 36.48→2535;
- continued at the foot: 0.49.20.52→2546, 40.52→2551, 0.50.8.40→2558.

The implicit reduction (mine) is T = Δt/Δn over long baselines:
- 128→2109: Δt = 7923.4 s, Δn = 1981, T = 3.99970 s.
- 2109→2529: 1679.8 s / 420 = 3.99952 s.
- 128→2535: 9627.28 s / 2407 = 3.99970 s.
- 128→2558: 9719.2 s / 2430 = 3.99967 s.
- Short-gap checks: 182→128 gives 216.08/54 = 4.0015 s. The 12 s or 8 s gaps for 3 or 2 units give 4.00 s.

SERIES II (S→N passages). The first line is 21h59m39.0s→0.5 (machine-read '4.59'), then:
- 51.0→3.5; 22.0.19.0→10.5;
- 22.5.19.8→85.5, 5.28.0→87.5;
- 22.7.3.8→111.5, 11.8→113.5;
- 22.9.3.4→141.5, 23.6→146.5;
- 0.21.20.6→2126, 32.6→2129, 44.68→2132 (machine-read '2004');
- continued at the foot: 0.56.54.16→2659.5, 57.14.16→2664.5, 26.16→2667.5.

The long-baseline periods (mine) are:
- 0.5→2126 (taken as 2125.5 units): 8501.6 s, T = 3.99981 s.
- 0.5→2667.5: 10667.16 s / 2667 = 3.99969 s.
- 85.5→111.5: 104 s / 26 = 4.0000 s.

'Elong. zu II' gives elongations, each with a scale reading, a time and a fractional count:
- 609 at 22.6.0.8 (95.75); 465 at 6.42.8 (106.25); 600 at 9.56.4 (154.75); 472 at 10.22.4 (161.25);
- 489 at 0.53.43.6 (2611.75); 624 at 54.45.2 (2627.25); 488 at 55.15.2 (2634.75); 626 at 56.1.2 (2646.25).

The counts follow from passage times at T = 4 s:
- (22.6.0.8 − 22.5.19.8)/4 = 10.25, so 85.5 + 10.25 = 95.75.
- (0.53.43.6 − 0.21.20.6)/4 = 1943/4 = 485.75, so 2126 + 485.75 = 2611.75.

The scale readings alternate between the two turning points, giving the amplitude and rest point.
- Early: mean rest ≈ 536.5, total arc ≈ 136 divisions.
- Late: rest ≈ 556.75, arc ≈ 136.5 divisions. Amplitude was therefore almost undamped over about 3 hours.

Result (implicit): both components oscillate with the same period, T ≈ 3.9997 s. The time ranges of I and II overlap, so they were observed simultaneously. This suggests one oscillating body (e.g. a pendulum) observed in two perpendicular directions, but this is my conjecture. The physical purpose (the bundle is 'Induktion') is not stated on the page.
errors: The I-entry machine-read '2009' must be 2109: it is consistent with 2111 and 2113 at 4 s steps and with the long-baseline period (2009 would give T = 4.21 s).
The I-entry machine-read '2537' must be 2533: 16 s after 2529 at 4 s per unit, and 2535 follows 8 s later.
The II-entry machine-read '2004' must be 2132 (12.08 s after 2129).
The II time machine-read '4.59.39,0' is 21.59.39,0 (it precedes 22.0.19,0).

Small internal inconsistency in II: 22.0.19.0 (10.5) to 22.5.19.8 (85.5) gives 300.8 s / 75 = 4.0107 s instead of 4.000. Either one of the early second-readings is off by about 0.8 s, or the count was slipped.

The phase labelling in II changes between half-integers (0.5 … 146.5; 2659.5 …) and integers (2126, 2129, 2132). In the early elongations the .75 turning point reads high (609, 600); in the late ones it reads low (489, 488). This implies a half-period shift in which turning point or passage was timed. It is either a deliberate convention change or a real phase change; the page does not explain it.
The late value 2659.5 at 0.56.54.16 computes to about 2659.4 from 2126 at T = 4 s, a deviation of about 0.4 s. This is within observing scatter.

results.what: Determination of an oscillation period by timing transits through the middle position, in groups, at widely separated epochs, and dividing elapsed time by elapsed swing count (T ≈ 3.9997 s for both components)
results.modern_name: Method of passages / long-baseline period determination (transit timing)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard astronomical-geophysical practice; refined in Gauss's and Weber's magnetometer work (1832–1837)

results.what: Elongation (turning-point) scale readings via mirror and telescope, interpolated at quarter-period phases, giving amplitude and rest point
results.modern_name: Poggendorff–Gauss mirror-and-scale reading of turning points

results.what: Simultaneous timing of E–W and S–N swing components with equal periods
results.modern_name: Two-component observation of an oscillating body (purpose unclear)

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine raw observation data with standard passage-timing and elongation reading. The reductions are implicit and elementary. The only curiosity is the simultaneous two-direction observation and the phase bookkeeping, whose purpose is not evident from this page.

transcription_corrections: The heading's 'bl. Augen' is an abbreviation of 'blossem Auge' (naked eye), parallel to II.
The last block mixes series I (2546, 2551, 2558 at 0.49–0.50) and series II (2659.5, 2664.5, 2667.5 at 0.56–0.57).
